newsitem.title: USA: Coke drops last teas from Fruitopia line.
newsitem.headline: Coke drops last teas from Fruitopia line.

text.p: The Coca-Cola Co said on Tuesday that it has decided to drop the last two tea drinks from its Fruitopia line in order to concentrate the brand exclusively on fruit flavors.

The two teas to be scrapped are Peaceable Peach and Born Raspberry. Their disappearance would reduced the number of Fruitopia products from an initial 12 flavors to four fruit drinks and two lemonades.
Coca-Cola spokesman Scott Jacobson said the move reflects the significant changes in consumer tastes that have taken place since the line first appeared three years ago.
Coca-Cola introduced Fruitopia as a challenge to Quaker Oats Co's Snapple brand soft-drinks, which include a dozen teas from a total of 50 flavors.

"The whole concept of New Age beverages is not what people thought it was a few years ago. We're not talking really about 'New Age' beverages, we're talking about a juice drink versus a ready-to-drink tea. It's all back to basics, I think, a little bit," Jacobson told Reuters.
Last year, Fruitopia sales were down overall because the company dropped six brand names from the line including two teas, Curious Mango Tea and Lemon Berry Intuition Tea.
But Jacobson said sales among Fruitopia's fruit-flavored beverages climbed 15 percent in the same period.
Coca-Cola, which transferred the peach- and raspberry-flavored teas to Fruitopia from its Nestea line in 1995, plans to reintroduce them as Nestea flavors this year.
Meanwhile, Jacobson said the changes did not mean the Fruitopia line lacked support from Coke management.

A new Fruitopia fruit flavor, Mind over Mango, was to be rolled out nationally later this year following market testing in the Southwest. And a second new fruit flavor already has entered testing phase for possible introduction in 1998.
